angle: Product and buyer side: utility and data-center trade press (T&D World, Data Center Frontier, DCD, Manufacturing Dive, Area Development, Plant Services), hyperscaler/colocation prefab supply-chain items, mobile-substation procurement items, then each supplier's own locations/manufacturing pages. No OSHA, NAICS-coded lists, EPA NAICS searches or welder postings used.
notes: Resumed run: searches 1-30 by the earlier DC-A run, 31-38 by this run (log in /tmp/claude-0/dc-audit-A/searches.jsonl). Dry point NOT reached: searches 32, 33, 35, 36 and 37 each still surfaced new supplier names (Faith Technologies El Paso, Intermountain Electronics, Elgin Power Solutions, Raptor, Roeslein, nVent, Compu Dynamics, Submer, Flex modules).

The earlier run saved page text but not URLs. URLs were re-established by direct fetch of company pages and publisher site-search boxes; where a URL could not be recovered, the row keeps the quote from the earlier saved page with url empty, quote_verified=false and flag 'url not recovered'. quote_check says whether the quote appears in the saved text.
quote_verified=true means tools/fetch_page.py --check found the quote on the live URL on 2026-11-19.

Row rules: in_definition=true when a fetched page states an in-definition product for the plant, or for a single-line company whose page places the site; multi-site companies whose page ties no in-definition product to a site are false with why_not 'site-level product not stated'. plant_confirmed follows only whether a page places fabrication/manufacturing at that city or address; operating status (pre-production) is carried in flags. City/state are 'unknown' unless a fetched page states them.

in_definition rules applied: integrators that outfit bought-in enclosures are out (Interstates Topeka uses PTMW enclosures; PTMW added as the fabricator); FRP-composite modules out (Northstar); cooling makers out unless a welded frame/skid is stated (Daikin, LiquidStack, XNRGY, FlaektGroup out; S&S Technical and Swanton in as stated skid makers); switchgear/PDU-only plants out (Vertiv Anderson, Raptor, Eaton Bellevue).
Duplicates: Flex Dallas power-pod facility is probably the same 400,000 sq ft building as Crown Technical Systems Dallas (duplicate_of set). Easter-Owens Arvada folded into Crusoe Arvada.

Unresolved leads (no US plant city found within two fetches): Forgent's other Minnesota site(s); Avail's other two plants; Crusoe Louisiana; Strick PA and SC; Vertiv's unnamed SC and PA additions; IEM plants (San Antonio lead unconfirmed); Hyper; GrayWolf Modular; Compu Dynamics Modular (Odessa TX lead unconfirmed); Intelliflex USA (Fort Worth, site unreachable); BMarko Structures (DNS failure); Servtech/Roeslein; Encore Electric fabrication; E&I Sales; Celestica modular electrical buildings (Fort Worth not tied to MEB); Jabil/Siemens Prince George VA; Socomec GA; Switchgear Power Systems LLC; Prince Manufacturing; ABB eHouse US site; Submer Corenix US site; Daikin's Modular Comfort Systems (NY); nVent control-building/mobile-substation plant; Elgin Power Solutions city (WV); Electronic Power Design plant city; Swanton Welding city; Rittal US plant; FTI Monroe LA and Excellerate's other Wisconsin sites (Little Chute is described as its fourth; faithtechinc.com gives no site list); LEI; BladeRoom USA (old); Coloaire (mock-up, unverified); GE Grid mobile substations (no US site); Fabcon; Eaton MITS (site unknown); Tate and Eagle Aluminum containment; Amco Enclosures, RackSolutions, Rackmount Solutions, Polargy/Forge Racks (403).

Seen and left out: Generac Sussex WI (generators, other vertical), Hammond Power (transformers), Rogers Brothers (trailers), AZZ mobile switchgear integration (old), Pioneer Power (trailer power), Wiwynn Socorro TX and Hyve (server integration), Trachte (fetched page shows self-storage buildings only), Schneider El Paso TX (custom electrical products, not prefab).

Blind spots of this method: welding is rarely stated by e-house/skid/rack makers, so most rows carry 'welding not stated'; trade press favours large, announced expansions, so small contract fabricators building skids and enclosures for integrators (like PTMW behind Interstates) are found only by chance; multi-plant companies often name only HQ or the new plant; the 8-search cap left the hyperscaler-supplier angle thin (search 31 found no named fabricator).
